digest.component_or_area: git workflow tooling / commit message amendment
propositions: git commit --amend -F <file> or --amend -m replaces the entire commit message and drops the Change-Id trailer, causing Gerrit's commit-msg hook to stamp a fresh Change-Id and open a duplicate change instead of a new patchset

A prepare-commit-msg hook cannot distinguish an amending -F invocation from a fresh -F commit because git reports identical hook metadata for both, making server-side or hook-based detection infeasible

Major Gerrit projects (Go, OpenStack, Android, Chromium) solve this by providing a documented wrapper command that amends while preserving the Change-Id, making the failure mode unreachable rather than detectable
A make amend-msg FILE=<path> wrapper must read HEAD's Change-Id, merge it into the amended message via git interpret-trailers, and fail loudly (non-zero exit) if HEAD carries no Change-Id
AGENTS.md documentation must explicitly state that --amend -m / --amend -F drop the Change-Id and create duplicate Gerrit changes, and recommend make amend-msg as the path for rewritten messages
